correctness.rationale: The two triangle equations imply x_{i+3}=x_i and y_i=x_{i+2} over every abelian group, and cap sums eliminate all solutions unless 3 divides n. This explicitly proves the torsion-free universal matrix invariant, all ordinary/generative criteria and finite counts. Strong labels correspond to distinct nonzero doubles in 2Γ[4], giving t²(r−1)(r−2) and exact C4² threshold; dihedral automorphisms act as all S3 permutations on triples, and Burnside gives the orbit formula. Full proof reconstructed for arbitrary abelian groups; independent finite direct face checks and integer Smith computations confirm all tested boundaries.

value.rationale: An entire natural family of 3-connected quartic polyhedral graphs exhibits an exact mod-three phase transition, and the theorem computes the universal integer facial constraint lattice and complete ordinary/strong symmetry-resolved counts. It sharpens the 2025 paper’s natural questions on strongly generative graph-group compatibility for a fixed infinite family, and does not merely restate the earlier subgroup necessity.
